question: Two cartons weigh the same, but one is much harder to handle. Which features of the carton itself could explain the difference?
reference_answer: It may be bulky, difficult to grip, slippery, sharp or unstable. Weight is only one feature of the load that affects manual handling.
answer:
If two cartons weigh the same, the difference in how hard they are to handle can be explained by their physical characteristics. According to health and safety guidance, a load may be considered unsuitable for manual handling if it is:

*   **Bulky or unwieldy:** Size and shape can make a load harder to manage, especially if it forces the handler to manipulate it at a distance from the trunk of the body [HSG76, p. 54].
*   **Slippery or wet:** These surface conditions affect the ability to get a secure grip [HSG76, p. 54].
*   **Sharp:** Sharp edges can make a load difficult or dangerous to handle [HSG76, p. 54].
*   **Unpredictable or unstable:** If the contents of a carton are not secure, the load may shift unexpectedly, which can take the handler by surprise [HSG76, p. 54; HSG76, p. 55].

Overloaded vehicles can become unstable, difficult to steer, and have less efficient braking. 138 Where a part of the load is to be picked up or removed in the course of a journey, the effect on gross weight, individual axle weights and on the securing and stability of the load must be taken into account. Although removal of part of the load will reduce the gross vehicle weight, the change in weight distribution may cause individual axles to become overloaded (often referred to as the diminishing load effect). 139 It is important to remember that the weight of the load itself will not be enough to prevent it moving – even heavy loads can move during transport. Friction alone cannot be relied on to keep the load in place. Anchor points 140 When loads are secured to a vehicle, the places where the load straps are attached are known as anchor points. Every driver needs to know how to deal with a load that has moved into an unsafe position. If the load appears to have shifted: • assess the safety, stability and security of the load before any restraints are removed; • quarantine the vehicle in a safe area, away from other work, until a competent person has decided on a safe system of work for unloading (a competent person is someone with the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to do the work safely); • do not open a bulging curtain on a curtain-sider as the load could fall out. Access the load compartment using another route, such as the back door or the curtain on the other side of the vehicle; • ask for help from the receiving employer or site operator if necessary.
